Taking ~23 cm as an effective diameter, the area is about 3.14 x 11.5^2 ≈ 415 cm^2 (a square plate of 22 cm per side would be about 480 cm^2 minus the corners, so ~415 is reasonable).

STEP 3 - Items: One red-green apple. No sauce or other food is visible.

STEP 4 - Area: The apple spans about 125 px against a plate width of about 390 px, so its diameter is about 7.4 cm. Its footprint is about 43 cm^2, roughly 10% of the plate. Food coverage in total is ~10%.

STEP 5 - Volume: A sphere of 7.4 cm diameter has a volume of about 0.52 x 7.4^3 ≈ 212 ml. The apple is slightly less than a perfect sphere, so ~200 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole apple density is about 0.85 g/ml, giving ~170 g. This matches a medium apple.

STEP 7 - Energy: Apple is about 52 kcal/100 g, so 170 g gives ~88 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A medium apple of ~170 g and ~90 kcal is plausible.
